import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_5/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_5/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join Source1_5_0 and Source1_5_1 on ProvinciaID
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="ProvinciaID", how="inner")

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID', 'ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre']
df_target = df_joined[['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID', 'ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre']]

# Ensure ProvinciaID, RegionID, ComunaID are integers
df_target['ProvinciaID'] = df_target['ProvinciaID'].astype(int)
df_target['RegionID'] = df_target['RegionID'].astype(int)
df_target['ComunaID'] = df_target['ComunaID'].astype(int)

# ProvinciaNombre and ComunaNombre should be strings without extra quotes
# Remove any leading/trailing quotes and whitespace
df_target['ProvinciaNombre'] = df_target['ProvinciaNombre'].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'").str.strip('"')
df_target['ComunaNombre'] = df_target['ComunaNombre'].astype(str).str.strip().str.strip("'").str.strip('"')

# Save the final target table to the specified path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1_5_0 and Source1_5_1 on ProvinciaID
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="ProvinciaID", how="inner")

# Group by all columns to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
# Since the target keys are ['ComunaNombre', 'ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre'] and the target schema is:
# ['ProvinciaID', 'ProvinciaNombre', 'RegionID', 'ComunaID', 'ComunaNombre']
# Grouping by all columns ensures no duplicates and respects keys.
grouped = joined.groupby(
    ["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"],
    as_index=False
).size()  # size() just to trigger groupby, but we don't need aggregation, so drop it

# The above .size() returns a Series with counts, but we don't want counts, just unique rows.
# So instead, just drop duplicates to match the target unique keys:
grouped = joined.drop_duplicates(subset=["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"])

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final = grouped[["ProvinciaID", "ProvinciaNombre", "RegionID", "ComunaID", "ComunaNombre"]]

# Write to output CSV
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_5/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
